question: In which type of forests are wild donkeys and camels found in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Thorny forests and bushes**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Wild donkeys and camels** in India are typically found in **Thorny forests and bushes**.
 
• These regions are characterized by **arid and semi-arid climates**, which are suitable for the survival of these animals.
 
• Thorny forests and bushes are primarily located in the **northwestern parts of India**, such as Rajasthan and Gujarat.
 
• The vegetation in these areas consists of **thorny trees, shrubs, and bushes** that can withstand harsh climatic conditions.
 
• These forests provide the necessary **habitat and food resources** for wild donkeys and camels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thorny forests** are also known as **desert vegetation** or **xerophytic vegetation**.
 
• These forests are adapted to **conserve water** and survive in low moisture conditions.
 
• Common plant species found in these forests include **acacias, cacti, and euphorbias**.
 
• The **Great Rann of Kutch** in Gujarat is a notable region where wild donkeys (Indian Wild Ass) are found.
 
• Conservation efforts are in place to protect the habitats of these species due to their ecological importance.
